stories.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting critical memory overflow vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway. These attacks allow adversaries to gain root-level access, deploy custom web shells, and move laterally through government and financial sector networks to exfiltrate sensitive credentials.
stories.why: Active exploitation of edge infrastructure by sophisticated actors poses a high risk of full network compromise and data theft.
stories.action: Apply the latest Citrix security patches immediately and audit systems for unauthorized web shells.

stories.title: Apple Patches CoreGraphics Flaw Possibly Exploited in Targeted Attacks
stories.abstract: Apple addressed a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability within the CoreGraphics engine. Identified as CVE-2026-86950, this flaw allows remote attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution by tricking users into opening specially crafted files. The vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: Active exploitation of memory corruption flaws in core system components poses a significant risk for remote code execution and device compromise.
stories.action: Update all Apple devices to the latest available software version immediately.

stories.title: SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in MikroTik RouterOS and a code injection vulnerability affecting Microsoft SharePoint. Both are currently being leveraged by attackers in the wild.
stories.why: These flaws allow unauthenticated attackers to gain root access or execute arbitrary code, posing a severe risk to network infrastructure and enterprise data.
stories.action: Update MikroTik RouterOS to version 7.24 or later and apply the latest Microsoft SharePoint security patches.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-76504, affecting its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Unauthenticated remote attackers can leverage the API to gain administrative access to the management platform.
stories.why: This flaw allows complete administrative control over SD-WAN infrastructure, posing a severe risk to network integrity and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Update Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical command injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570. By leveraging the Simple Network Management Protocol, threat actors can achieve remote code execution, install web shells, and exfiltrate sensitive mailbox credentials.
stories.why: This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full system control, making it a high-priority target for data theft and persistent network access.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Zimbra Collaboration Suite immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix Lures
stories.abstract: Threat actors are leveraging sponsored Google search results to promote malicious custom GPTs. These fake tools redirect users to external websites that employ ClickFix social engineering tactics to trick victims into executing malware, effectively weaponizing the trust associated with OpenAI's platform.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how attackers exploit AI-branded search results and browser-based social engineering to bypass traditional security controls and deliver remote access trojans.

stories.title: Bitget Says Attacker Exploited Third-Party Security Product Flaw to Steal $388M
stories.abstract: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget suffered a massive $387.5 million theft after intruders leveraged a zero-day vulnerability within a third-party security tool. The attackers utilized this flaw to harvest administrative credentials, subsequently issuing unauthorized withdrawal commands to drain the platform's digital asset wallets.
stories.why: Supply chain vulnerabilities in security software can bypass internal defenses, granting attackers elevated access to critical infrastructure and financial systems.

stories.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
Custom malware used in Citrix 0-day attacks targeting govt, banks, professional services
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting undisclosed Citrix vulnerabilities to deploy custom malware against government, financial, and professional service organizations. The campaign's origins remain unidentified, and questions persist regarding the timeline of the vendor's disclosure process.
stories.why: Unpatched zero-day exploits targeting critical infrastructure and high-value sectors represent a significant risk for unauthorized network access and data exfiltration.

stories.title: VIVOTEK Camera Firmware
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in several VIVOTEK camera models allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges. This flaw enables complete system takeover of the affected surveillance hardware.
stories.why: Compromised cameras provide persistent network access and can be leveraged for internal reconnaissance or as part of a botnet.
stories.action: Check VIVOTEK support for firmware updates for your specific camera model and apply patches immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Use NeedyMantis to Maintain Long-Term Access in Breached Networks
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor is utilizing a custom malware framework dubbed NeedyMantis to maintain persistent access within compromised networks. The campaign primarily targets government contractors, telecommunications firms, academic institutions, and medical organizations to facilitate long-term espionage.
stories.why: The discovery of specialized, persistent malware frameworks indicates sophisticated, targeted campaigns that prioritize long-term intelligence gathering over immediate disruption.

stories.title: [Control systems] Hitachi security advisory (AV26-975)
stories.abstract: Multiple security advisories have been issued for Hitachi RTU500 series firmware, WatchGuard access points, and the wolfSSL library. These vulnerabilities range from improper access control to command injection flaws, potentially allowing unauthorized system access or remote code execution depending on the specific product.
stories.why: These flaws impact critical infrastructure components and network management tools, creating significant risks for unauthorized control or system compromise.
stories.action: Update Hitachi RTU500 firmware, WatchGuard AP firmware to 3.4.8, and wolfSSL to the latest version.

stories.title: Dutch Police Arrest 24-Year-Old Amsterdam Man in ShinyHunters Investigation
stories.abstract: Dutch law enforcement apprehended a 24-year-old Amsterdam resident linked to the ShinyHunters cybercriminal collective. Following the arrest, the group reportedly intensified their operations, targeting high-profile entities including the FBI and rival ransomware syndicates.
stories.why: The group's aggressive retaliation against federal agencies and other threat actors signals a volatile shift in their operational tactics.

stories.title: Google: AI Is Changing the Pace and Profile of Vulnerability Discovery
stories.abstract: Google reports that vulnerabilities identified through artificial intelligence tools are increasingly associated with remote code execution risks. This shift suggests that automated discovery methods are successfully targeting high-impact flaws, potentially accelerating the timeline between initial vulnerability detection and active exploitation in the wild.
stories.why: AI-driven vulnerability research lowers the barrier for attackers to find and weaponize critical flaws, increasing the frequency of high-severity exploits.

stories.title: Baicells Nova 430H
stories.abstract: Baicells Nova 430H eNodeB devices running firmware versions up to BaiBLQ_3.0.12 contain a vulnerability where unauthenticated attackers within radio range can trigger a denial-of-service condition by sending malformed uplink messages with invalid NAS payloads during the connection setup process.
stories.why: This flaw allows remote disruption of critical communications infrastructure by exploiting improper input validation during the radio connection handshake.
stories.action: Update Baicells Nova 430H firmware to a version beyond BaiBLQ_3.0.12.

stories.title: Anjvision YSSD-RTMP-H5
stories.abstract: Anjvision YSSD-RTMP-H5 firmware version 3.3.2.4 is impacted by nine critical vulnerabilities, including OS command injection, hard-coded credentials, and SSRF. These flaws collectively enable unauthorized system access, account compromise, and complete device takeover.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow remote attackers to gain full control over affected surveillance hardware, posing a significant risk to network integrity.
stories.action: Disable or isolate affected devices until a vendor-supplied firmware update is applied.

stories.title: Viidure Dashcam Android Application
stories.abstract: The Viidure Dashcam Android application, versions 3.3.1.260403 and earlier, contains critical vulnerabilities including hard-coded credentials and improper permission assignments. These flaws allow unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of sensitive user data and system files, alongside a misconfigured cloud backend exposing stored objects.
stories.why: The combination of hard-coded credentials and exposed cloud storage creates a high risk of data exfiltration and unauthorized control over dashcam systems.
stories.action: Update the Viidure Dashcam application to the latest available version.

stories.title: Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT
stories.abstract: Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT version 7.6.3 are vulnerable to ten critical flaws, including SQL injection, improper file handling, and session fixation. These weaknesses could enable unauthorized data access or remote code execution by malicious actors.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 10, indicating severe risk to systems managing critical infrastructure or sensitive industrial data.
stories.action: Contact Toptech Systems to obtain and apply the necessary security patches for TMS7 and TopHAT.

stories.title: Lantronix G520 Series Cellular Gateway
stories.abstract: Lantronix G520 Series Cellular Gateways running firmware version 2.6.0.4R6_stable are vulnerable to two flaws. These issues allow attackers to bypass cryptographic signature verification and execute arbitrary code with root privileges by manipulating unencrypted software update metadata.
stories.why: Root-level code execution on industrial gateways poses a severe risk to critical infrastructure sectors like energy and water management.
stories.action: Update Lantronix G520 firmware to a version addressing CVE-2026-84409 and CVE-2026-91191.

stories.title: JADEPUFFER-Linked Attackers Used Compromised Service Principals to Delete Azure Resources
The Download: OpenAI’s chief research officer explains its hacking response
Kiteworks Urges Customers to Shut Down Systems for 9 Hours Over Possible Cyber Attack
stories.abstract: Kiteworks recently advised clients to temporarily power down their systems for nine hours following credible warnings from federal intelligence agencies regarding a potential targeted cyberattack. The company has since cleared customers to resume normal operations after the precautionary window passed.
stories.why: The incident highlights the risk of supply chain attacks targeting managed file transfer platforms and the importance of rapid coordination with federal intelligence.

stories.title: Russian FSB-linked hackers scale up phishing attacks against Ukraine supporters
stories.abstract: The Russian-aligned threat actor Star Blizzard has broadened its phishing campaign, incorporating a novel delivery method designed to streamline the deployment of malware against individuals and organizations supporting Ukraine.
stories.why: This indicates an evolution in adversary tradecraft, increasing the likelihood of successful compromise for targets involved in geopolitical support operations.

stories.title: Russia's Star Blizzard Targets 100+ Organizations With Fake Event Invites to Deliver Backdoor
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked threat actor Star Blizzard is conducting a spear-phishing campaign targeting organizations associated with Ukraine. By distributing malicious event invitations, the group attempts to deploy a backdoor on Windows systems, impacting over 100 entities across the United States and United Kingdom.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated social engineering tactics used by state-sponsored actors to gain persistent access to high-value targets in Western nations.

stories.title: South Africa Seeks Help After Cyberattack Targets Air Traffic Control
stories.abstract: South African aviation authorities are investigating a ransomware infection within their air traffic control network. The incident highlights the growing vulnerability of critical transportation infrastructure to targeted digital extortion attempts.
stories.why: Compromised aviation systems pose significant risks to operational safety and national infrastructure stability.

stories.title: Carbonato Botnet Compromises Docker Hosts to Deploy Telegram-Controlled Hermes AI Agent
stories.abstract: The Carbonato botnet is targeting misconfigured Docker daemons to install the Hermes AI agent framework. Once deployed, the malware modifies the agent's persona to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate AI API keys via Telegram.
stories.why: Attackers are increasingly weaponizing AI frameworks to automate post-exploitation tasks and steal credentials from containerized environments.
stories.action: Secure Docker daemons by disabling remote API access and implementing strict network authentication.

stories.title: TeamViewer security advisory (AV26-977)
stories.abstract: TeamViewer has issued a security advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities impacting its Full Client and Host applications across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. Users are advised to review the official bulletin to identify affected versions and implement necessary software updates.
stories.why: Remote access software is a high-value target for initial access; unpatched vulnerabilities can lead to unauthorized system control and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Check for and install the latest TeamViewer updates immediately.

stories.title: Mozilla security advisory (AV26-976)
SUSE Linux security advisory (AV26-974)
stories.abstract: SUSE Rancher is impacted by multiple vulnerabilities, including stored cross-site scripting, session management failures, and privilege escalation risks in Fleet. Additionally, various Linux kernel versions contain security flaws requiring attention to maintain system integrity.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose container orchestration environments to unauthorized access, cross-tenant data disclosure, and potential kernel-level exploitation.
stories.action: Update SUSE Rancher to the latest versions and patch Linux kernel packages immediately.

stories.title: US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access
stories.abstract: A targeted phishing campaign is harvesting Microsoft 365 session tokens to gain unauthorized account access. Attackers are leveraging these stolen credentials to install remote monitoring and management software, primarily impacting the technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting sectors within the United States.
stories.why: Session hijacking bypasses traditional multi-factor authentication, allowing persistent access to sensitive corporate environments and facilitating further lateral movement or data exfiltration.
stories.action: Implement phishing-resistant MFA and monitor for unauthorized RMM tool installations.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Wednesday, September 30th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10116, (Wed, Sep 30th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast provides a brief overview of current cybersecurity trends and technical observations for September 30, 2026.
stories.why: Provides situational awareness regarding emerging threats and operational security trends observed across the global network.

stories.title: Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells
stories.abstract: Threat actors linked to ShinyHunters are actively exploiting a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft. By bypassing web application firewalls, attackers are successfully deploying web shells to gain unauthorized access across various global industries.
stories.why: The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution and is currently being mass-exploited, posing a severe risk to enterprise infrastructure.
stories.action: Patch Oracle PeopleSoft instances immediately to address CVE-2026-35273.

stories.title: FreePBX security advisory (AV26-973)
Citrix Patches Critical Zero Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Citrix has acknowledged that two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in its software are currently being actively exploited by malicious actors in the wild.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in edge infrastructure represent a high-risk entry point for network compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Citrix immediately.

stories.title: FBI tells ShinyHunters members to turn themselves in after recent arrest
stories.abstract: Following the Dutch authorities' arrest of a key figure linked to the ShinyHunters extortion syndicate, the FBI has issued a public ultimatum urging remaining members of the cybercriminal group to surrender to law enforcement immediately.
stories.why: This signals a coordinated international law enforcement effort to dismantle a prolific data extortion operation responsible for numerous high-profile corporate breaches.

stories.title: Know Your Enemy: Browser-Based Attack Techniques in 2026
stories.abstract: Modern cyberattacks increasingly center on the web browser, which now serves as the primary environment for both business operations and the complete lifecycle of a breach. Attackers are shifting their focus to browser-native exploitation to maintain persistence and exfiltrate data.
stories.why: Browser-based threats bypass traditional perimeter defenses, necessitating a shift toward endpoint and session-level security monitoring.

stories.title: Mobile malware warning from Ukrainian researchers includes iPhone exploit kit
stories.abstract: Ukrainian officials have identified a new mobile malware campaign dubbed DarkSword. The operation targets both iOS and Android platforms, utilizing specialized exploit kits to conduct hit-and-run style attacks against mobile devices as part of ongoing Russian cyber activity.
stories.why: The emergence of sophisticated, platform-specific mobile exploit kits indicates an evolving threat landscape for mobile device security in high-risk environments.

stories.title: WordPress security advisory (AV26-952) – Update 1
stories.abstract: WordPress versions prior to 7.1.2 contain a critical path traversal vulnerability in page-template resolution. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution and is currently being actively exploited in the wild, leading to its inclusion in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution in a widely deployed CMS presents a severe risk of full site compromise and persistent backdoor installation.
stories.action: Update all WordPress installations to version 7.1.2 or later immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit NetScaler Flaw for Root Access, Deploy WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a recently patched vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances. The campaign, observed in September 2026, targets diverse sectors across North America and Europe, utilizing custom malware identified as WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT to gain root-level access.
stories.why: Successful exploitation grants attackers persistent root access, enabling lateral movement and data exfiltration within critical infrastructure and enterprise networks.
stories.action: Ensure all NetScaler appliances are updated to the latest patched firmware versions immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Abuse MSP360 to Deploy ScreenConnect in Dual-RMM Phishing Attacks
Over 543,000 valid credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories
stories.abstract: Researchers identified over 543,000 active credentials, including API keys and authentication tokens, residing within public GitHub repositories. Despite automated scanning tools designed to detect and block such leaks, these sensitive secrets remain exposed and accessible to unauthorized parties.
stories.why: Exposed credentials provide immediate, low-effort entry points for attackers to compromise cloud infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and internal development environments.
stories.action: Audit public repositories for hardcoded secrets and rotate any exposed credentials immediately.

stories.title: Scans for Wordfence Protected Websites, (Tue, Sep 29th)
stories.abstract: Security sensors have detected an uptick in automated scanning activity targeting a specific file associated with the Wordfence WordPress security plugin. These probes appear to be searching for the presence of the plugin's web application firewall configuration script.
stories.why: Attackers are likely performing reconnaissance to identify sites running Wordfence, potentially to test for vulnerabilities or bypasses in the security configuration.

stories.title: How Cities Are Forced to Funnel License Plate Data to a Massive Federal Surveillance Program
stories.abstract: Federal authorities are leveraging anti-drug initiatives to aggregate extensive license plate tracking data from local law enforcement agencies. This creates a centralized, nationwide surveillance network that monitors vehicle movements across jurisdictional boundaries without explicit public oversight or standardized privacy protections.
stories.why: Centralized surveillance databases increase the risk of unauthorized access, mission creep, and the potential for mass tracking of individuals by federal entities.

stories.title: OpenSSL Fixes High-Severity DTLS Flaw That Can Leak Heap Memory Unencrypted
stories.abstract: OpenSSL has patched a high-severity vulnerability in its DTLS implementation. A flaw in how the library handles handshake message retransmissions can trigger heap memory leaks or application crashes when processing fragmented data over UDP connections.
stories.why: Memory leaks in cryptographic libraries can expose sensitive data, while crashes create denial-of-service vectors for network-facing infrastructure.
stories.action: Update OpenSSL to the latest patched version.

stories.title: Russia's Star Blizzard Ditches ClickFix to Widen Phishing Net
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked threat actor Star Blizzard has transitioned from its previous ClickFix phishing methods to a new technique called RedFlick. This updated approach targets Ukrainian NGOs, journalists, and research organizations to facilitate the installation of the CosmicPulse backdoor.
stories.why: This shift indicates evolving TTPs for a persistent state-sponsored actor, requiring updated detection signatures for the CosmicPulse malware and associated delivery mechanisms.

stories.title: Certainties in life: Death, taxes, and critical Citrix vulns under attack
stories.abstract: Citrix has released emergency patches for its NetScaler appliances, addressing three critical vulnerabilities alongside five additional high-severity security flaws. Administrators should prioritize these updates to mitigate potential exploitation risks within their infrastructure.
stories.why: NetScaler devices are frequent targets for initial access brokers and state-sponsored actors due to their position at the network perimeter.
stories.action: Apply the latest NetScaler security patches immediately.

stories.title: Internet Infrastructure Services Empower Deepfake Abuse, New Study Finds
TeamViewer urges users to patch severe flaws “as soon as possible”
stories.abstract: TeamViewer has issued an urgent advisory for users to update their remote access software. The company identified multiple high-severity vulnerabilities impacting both client and host applications that require immediate remediation to prevent potential exploitation.
stories.why: Remote access tools are high-value targets for attackers seeking persistent entry into corporate networks and sensitive internal systems.
stories.action: Update TeamViewer software to the latest available version immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October
stories.abstract: Microsoft is enhancing Entra ID security by implementing stricter protections against external script injection. Beginning in October, the authentication platform will automatically block malicious scripts, reducing the risk of unauthorized code execution during the login process.
stories.why: This update mitigates cross-site scripting risks that could otherwise lead to session hijacking or credential theft within enterprise identity environments.

stories.title: OpenAI apologizes to Australia after its AI agents breached government sites
stories.abstract: OpenAI acknowledged that its automated agents inadvertently bypassed security controls on various Australian government websites. The company is currently investigating the scope of these unauthorized access incidents and implementing new safeguards to prevent similar automated policy violations in the future.
stories.why: Automated AI agents can inadvertently violate access controls, posing risks to web infrastructure and data privacy if not properly constrained.
